description.narrative:
Oxfam/Somalia is implementing a programme in Somalia with the goal of amplifying and supporting voices of the most vulnerable groups and their capacity within the context of the climate emergency hence implementing this locally led climate action and climate education
The objective of this is to capacitate young people and students at university level to equip them necessary skills and knowledge around climate change / justice through creation of Climate education platforms, debates, and peer-peer learning. This initiative will enhance young Somalia students’ knowledge and skills necessary to bring lasting change and resilience to their communities. The Youth and the academia should spearhead active, bottom-up, people-driven Climate movement through various methods based on digital communication, including collaborative tools and Social Medias, to ensure the voices of excluded communities are heard
The Climate education includes:
- Community support through climate awareness and education. - Media relations - Media engagement – Climate change story from Youth, Activist, and women to share their experience around climate change / justice. - Professional learning; Workshop / Seminars / events. - Networking sessions -beer -beer learning – Collective Visioning focusing on Climate justice and connectwith other activist to create space for dialogues and debates around climate change. - Tree planting initiatives at school and community level.
The locally led climate action includes:
•Promote locally led actions to enable CBOs, CSOs and Youth led organizations to take up more leadership role in climate action in Somalia (Galmudug and Jubaland States). • Facilitate the development of climate narrative that reflects the experience, challengesand solutions of communities affected by climate change. • To advocate for local led solutions, strengthening the voices of those most affected by climate shocks. • Foster knowledge sharing and with diverse groups including activist, Youth lead and women groups, Grassroots Communities and involve them in Climate actions efforts.

participating-org.narrative: CPD is a Non-Profit, Non-Government Organization (NGO) founded in 2003 and registered in Somalia with the Federal Government and the various Regional Authorities in the areas it operates. The organization has 5 operational offices namely in Mogadishu city, Baidoatown, Galkaio, Hobyo town, Adado town and a liaison office in Nairobi (Kenya). CPD’s original mandate was to solely build peace, reduce conflicts, promote human rights, advance good governance and democratization. However, in 2007, the organization expanded its scope to include humanitarian assistance, poverty reduction through socio-economic development for the communities it serves and supporting the country’s stabilization initiatives as a measure to respond to the prevailing needs of the communities. The organization is under the overall management of the Board made up of Directors. The organization’s daily management is under the Senior Management Team consisting of 10 members including 9 line Managers and the Executive Director who is in charge of the team. CPD has a diverseand qualified human resource base consisting of 113 staff as of September 2018. 2.0 Vision: CPD envisions a poverty-free and sustainably-developed Africa. 3.0 Mission: To facilitate evidenced-based and participatory approaches to development for the sustained welfare of African communities.
